name: World State Flags
description: The world's memory of what you changed: the bridge stays repaired, the warlord stays dead, the gate stays open. A flag is a named boolean-or-value with a settable or set-once policy and a query interface everything else reads — doors, spawners, dialogue conditions. ui.dialogue_tree_engine writes consequence flags here rather than keeping them, because a consequence that dies with the conversation is a consequence the world forgot. persistence.save_system owns the bytes; this component owns the semantics — namespacing, defaults, and the rule that clearing a story flag is an explicit act, never a side effect of some other system's cleanup.

inputs.name: flagDefinitions
inputs.description: Known flags with defaults and set-once policies. Declaring flags up front turns typo'd flag names from silent quest-breakers into load-time errors.

inputs.name: namespaceBy
inputs.description: How flag names partition: zone | global | faction. Namespacing keeps two zones' 'bridge_repaired' from colliding into one confusing bridge.

inputs.name: strictUnknownFlagReads
inputs.description: Whether reading an undeclared flag throws instead of returning null. Strict in development, lenient in production — a shipped game should degrade, not crash.

outputs.name: flagCount
outputs.description: How many flags diverge from defaults — a save-size proxy.
